Build the rebuilt grant file from the downloaded extracts

Source: R/efilepf.R
pf_efilepf_build.Rd

Reads one year at a time and appends, so peak memory is one year (~2M rows) rather than the whole 17.5M-row table.

Usage

pf_efilepf_build(
  dir = pf_efilepf_dir(),
  out,
  years = pf_efilepf_years(),
  schema = c("v2", "gtdc"),
  dedup = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

dir

Directory holding the downloaded CSVs.

out

Output CSV path.

years

Years to include.

schema

"v2" for the published concordance990 names and full metadata, "gtdc" for the legacy v1 names.

dedup

Drop superseded and duplicate filings with pf_efilepf_dedup(). Requires schema = "v2", since the legacy schema discards the flags the rule needs.

verbose

Print progress.

Value

A one-row-per-year data.frame of counts, invisibly.

Details

Two e-file columns are carried through in addition to the GTDC schema, because they are free here and the GTDC file had no equivalent: OBJECTID, which identifies the source return, and efile_year, the extract the row came from (distinct from TAXYEAR when a return is filed late or amended).

Schema

schema = "v2" (the default) keeps the ef2 columns as published, with their concordance990 v2 names (PF_15_G_PAID_*) and the full filing metadata. schema = "gtdc" reproduces the legacy behaviour: rename to the v1 GTDC names via pf_efilepf_map() and keep only those columns.

The legacy path exists to reproduce artifacts built before the migration. It is a downgrade: the published files already carry the current names, and renaming them to v1 also discarded ten standardized columns. Two of those matter beyond tidiness — TABLE_ID, the within-filing row counter that makes OBJECTID + TABLE_ID a unique row key, and RETURN_AMENDED_X / RETURN_PARTIAL_X, without which superseded filings cannot be identified. Dropping TABLE_ID is why a content hash once had to be invented for a key the data already published.
